assessment_summary: I reviewed the guide and installation summary, then inspected the live environment at /workspace rather than relying on file existence. I confirmed the exact pinned runtimes (Ruby 3.1.4, Node 20.11.0, PostgreSQL 14.24), that Bundler dependencies are satisfied, and that both the development and test databases exist with 262 tables each. I queried the seeded data and matched the guide's stated admin/role users. I confirmed the documented server command is actually running (Puma 5.6.8 on 127.0.0.1:3000 in development) and exercised it over HTTP: home, proposals, debates, polls, projekts, and sign-in pages all return 200, including asset delivery. I performed real authentication with the documented admin credentials and role accounts and confirmed authenticated access to /admin (200). Most importantly, I drove a complete participation workflow: the app's own UI links to a project-scoped new-proposal form, which I submitted, producing a 302 redirect and a persisted proposal (id 76) whose detail page returns 200. This demonstrates the software is operational, not merely present. I also confirmed Rails boots in the test environment and that bin/rails and bin/rake work. The negative findings are non-blocking: the documented plain `bin/rspec` binstub fails due to a mutex_m default-gem/bundler conflict but runs correctly with the in-environment workaround DISABLE_SPRING=1 (or bundle exec rspec), requiring no install or repair; the many spec failures are caused by stale committed specs/factories referencing removed model APIs, a pre-existing condition of commit 5c3c7e1 unrelated to installation; and a bare GET /proposals/new without a projekt_phase_id raises 500 in an unmodified view that the UI never links to. Because the guide's deliverable (a seeded, running development instance exercising the participation platform) is demonstrated operationally and the remaining issues are pre-existing code/test conditions or tooling wrinkles with available workarounds rather than missing installation work, I assess the installation as successful. Uncertainty remains only around the breadth of pre-existing test-suite failures, which I attribute to repository state rather than the installation.
